decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blastoise. Pelipper + Snorlax lead establishes rain automatically and begins Curse while avoiding the poor Houndoom + Pelipper opening. Houndoom is the necessary Gengar check in back; Mega Blastoise becomes the rain-powered closer once Gengar is removed or pressured. Keep Snorlax away from Hydrapple until then.
decisions.notebook: Against this roster, continue preferring Pelipper + Snorlax as the opening when Houndoom can be preserved as the Mega Gengar check. Mega Blastoise is viable only with that Gengar pressure and should be treated as a rain-powered closer, not an early Thunderbolt target. Aerodactyl may replace its usual Rock Slide pressure with Tailwind when given a free turn. Hydrapple remains the preferred late pivot and Snorlax should avoid it until Gengar is gone. Snorlax's Curse plus Body Slam paralysis remains the route through Arcanine and Empoleon.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Mega Gengar. Gengar and Aerodactyl lead together to neutralize opposing offensive pressure: Wide Guard completely shuts down Blastoise's Water Spout and Tauros/Snorlax's Earthquake, while Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag traps Pelipper/Blastoise and threatens KOes with fast Thunderbolt. Empoleon punished Tauros's Intimidate via Competitive and resists Ice/Water coverage, while Hydrapple handles Water/Ground moves and pressures Toxapex and Snorlax with Earth Power and Giga Drain.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Blastoise-Mega (Water Spout), Pelipper (Drizzle/Hydro Pump), Houndoom (Life Orb), Snorlax (Thick Fat/Curse/Rest), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Intimidate), Toxapex (Kasib Berry/Haze/TSpikes). Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl lead heavily pressures their rain/fire core via fast Wide Guard (blocking Water Spout/EQ) and Shadow Tag + Thunderbolt coverage. Empoleon deters Intimidate with Competitive; Hydrapple walls rain attacks.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper must Protect to block the 4x SE Thunderbolt from faster Gengar (Gengar outspeeds and 90 BP STAB 4x SE is a guaranteed OHKO). Snorlax Curses safely since Aerodactyl Taunt is rare turn 1; Snorlax easily eats neutral Rock Slide and pivots if Taunted. Preserves rain for late Mega Blastoise sweep and Houndoom pivot into Gengar.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Aerodactyl lead confirmed; Gengar will likely Mega turn 1 for Shadow Tag, so avoid switching Pelipper out. Aerodactyl carries Taunt but standard is Rock Slide or Tailwind. Houndoom (Flash Fire, Life Orb, Sludge Bomb 2x SE) remains the planned switch-in once Gengar commits to Mega.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Gengar)
decisions.rationale: Gengar's Thunderbolt guarantees an OHKO on Pelipper (124-243%). Snorlax's only damage against Gengar is Earthquake (Gengar is immune to Body Slam); Aerodactyl's +3 priority Wide Guard completely blocks Earthquake, making Gengar completely safe while removing Pelipper. Mega Evolving traps the opponent with Shadow Tag.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Blastoise-Mega (Water Spout), Pelipper (Drizzle/Hydro Pump), Houndoom (Life Orb), Snorlax (Thick Fat/Curse/Rest), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Intimidate), Toxapex (Kasib Berry/Haze/TSpikes). Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl lead heavily pressures rain/fire core via fast Wide Guard and Shadow Tag + Thunderbolt coverage. Snorlax only threatens Gengar with Earthquake.

decisions.rationale: Hydro Pump is super effective into Aerodactyl and acts before likely Tailwind value, while Snorlax switches to Houndoom to preserve its boosted endgame and avoid Earthquake ally damage. This pressures Aerodactyl without exposing Pelipper to another immediate Thunderbolt/Rock Slide line.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega and Aerodactyl are the opponent's confirmed lead; Gengar has committed Mega Evolution and may enable Shadow Tag. Opponent has used Wide Guard once and Gengar has targeted Pelipper with Thunderbolt. Houndoom remains the planned switch-in after Gengar commits to Mega, with Flash Fire and Life Orb Sludge Bomb pressure. Preserve Snorlax's Curse-boosted endgame when practical.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Shadow Tag blocks Houndoom pivot; must break Gengar to free switches. Pelipper Protects (reduced 50% rate) to survive likely Tbolt OHKO and keep rain alive. Snorlax Curse-boosted Earthquake hits Gengar SE (Poison weak to Ground, 40-122%) for possible OHKO. Best case: Pelipper survives + Gengar dies = rain + Shadow Tag broken. Worst case: Pelipper dies but EQ high roll still KOs Gengar.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag confirmed; Houndoom swap blocked until Gengar dies. Aerodactyl used Wide Guard T1 (likely anticipating spreads). Pelipper rain critical for Blastoise-Mega WaterSpout + future pivots. Snorlax has Curse +1Atk/+1Def/-1Spe — preserve as wallbreaker. Plan to break Gengar next turn to pivot Houndoom in safely.

decisions.rationale: Houndoom is the safer forced replacement: it is not weak to Thunderbolt, whereas Blastoise would take a super-effective hit before acting. Houndoom also threatens Gengar with listed Dark Pulse next turn; once Gengar falls, Shadow Tag ends and future pivots reopen.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag confirmed; prioritize removing it to reopen switching. Aerodactyl repeatedly uses Wide Guard against spread pressure, so exploit it with listed single-target attacks when possible. Preserve Blastoise-Mega for rain Water Spout endgames; intended Mega is Blastoise. Snorlax's boosted Earthquake is blocked by Wide Guard and cannot hit Aerodactyl; Body Slam cannot hit Gengar. Houndoom's listed Dark Pulse is the planned single-target pressure into Gengar.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Gengar-Mega)
decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega's Thunderbolt guarantees an OHKO on Pelipper (150-293%). Wide Guard completely blocks Snorlax's only threat to Gengar-Mega (+1 Earthquake), ensuring Gengar-Mega takes no damage while removing the rain enabler under Shadow Tag.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Blastoise-Mega, Pelipper, Houndoom, Snorlax (Thick Fat/Curse/Rest/BodySlam/EQ), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Toxapex. Lead Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl with Wide Guard completely shuts down Snorlax's Earthquake coverage and traps key targets.

decisions.rationale: Houndoom Dark Pulse is the only single-target SE move into Gengar that bypasses Wide Guard and applies real Shadow Tag pressure (52-178% range). Snorlax Body Slam on Aerodactyl bypasses Wide Guard and chips the sash user. Aerodactyl Rock Slide can OHKO Houndoom, but Blastoise-Mega Water Spout in rain is the recovery plan if Houndoom goes down. Protecting wastes a critical Gengar-pressure turn.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag confirmed: cannot switch until it faints. Aerodactyl repeatedly uses Wide Guard — single-target moves bypass it. Rain lasts 3 more turns; intended Blastoise-Mega Water Spout endgame if Houndoom falls. Snorlax Curse +1/+1 already applied; another Curse gives +2/+2/-2 if needed. Houndoom Life Orb Dark Pulse is the main Gengar-Mega KO threat (SE 2x, single-target). Aerodactyl Focus Sash revealed; needs two hits to KO. Body Slam cannot hit Gengar-Mega (immune); Earthquake blocked by Wide Guard and would hit Houndoom ally.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Gengar cannot single-handedly OHKO Houndoom with Thunderbolt (22-72.7%), leaving it exposed to a high-roll LO Dark Pulse OHKO. Protect completely scout/blocks Houndoom while Aerodactyl (Sash intact, immune to Snorlax's Earthquake) lands Rock Slide to heavily chip or KO Houndoom. Shadow Tag prevents Houndoom from escaping.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Blastoise-Mega, Pelipper (fainted), Houndoom (LO), Snorlax (Thick Fat/Curse/Rest/BodySlam/EQ), Tauros-Paldea-Blaze, Toxapex. Lead Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl with Wide Guard completely shuts down Snorlax's Earthquake coverage and traps key targets.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving this turn and firing Dark Pulse at Gengar-Mega is the tempo play: Mega Launcher boosts Dark Pulse to a likely OHKO (77-142% range, ~75% OHKO chance on typical min-SpD Gengar-Mega) which removes Shadow Tag immediately. Even if Gengar survives at low HP, Blastoise takes only 60-71% from T-bolt (not OHKO) so it stays alive at 29-40%. Snorlax Body Slam likely KOs Aerodactyl from 47% HP. Single-target Dark Pulse bypasses Aerodactyl's Wide Guard. Plan A's Protect preserves HP but delays
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag confirmed; cannot switch until it faints. Aerodactyl Focus Sash listed but never activated (only triggers at full HP) - Body Slam on 47% HP can break through normally. RainDance 2 turns left. T-bolt on Mega Blastoise: 60.2-71% (survives easily, NOT an OHKO - earlier memory of 168-198 was wrong; tool estimate is authoritative). Mega Dark Pulse on Gengar-Mega with Launcher: 77-142% range (likely OHKO). Body Slam on Aero from 47%: 29.4-57.4% (likely KO, not guaranteed). Mega Water Spout in rain on Gengar: 80-148% but blocked by Wide Guard. Cross-game: plan to bring Empoleon/Dragonite after Gengar faints for Steel/Flying resists. Pelipper Drizzle + Houndoom Life Orb are gone; no other rain setters. Snorlax ThickFat checks Ice/Fire; with Curse already +1/+1, second Curse gives +2/+2 if needed.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Gengar-Mega)
decisions.rationale: Both foes rely heavily on powerful spread moves (Rain-boosted Water Spout from Mega Blastoise and +1 Earthquake from Snorlax). Aerodactyl's priority Wide Guard completely neutralizes both spread attacks. Gengar-Mega outspeeds Blastoise and lands a super-effective Thunderbolt, severely weakening or KOing Blastoise while remaining safe from Water Spout. Snorlax cannot touch Gengar with Normal attacks due to Ghost typing.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster: Blastoise-Mega, Pelipper (fainted), Houndoom (LO, fainted), Snorlax (Thick Fat/Curse/Rest/BodySlam/EQ). Lead Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl with Wide Guard completely shuts down Snorlax's Earthquake and Blastoise's Water Spout.

decisions.rationale: Both Gengar and Aerodactyl fainted on Turn 4, so both remaining bench Pokémon (Empoleon and Hydrapple) must be sent out. Sending Empoleon to Slot 1 and Hydrapple to Slot 2 fills the active slots.

Ice Beam moves before Hydrapple and threatens its 4x weakness; Earthquake pressures Empoleon super effectively. If neither Protects, this can remove both foes. If Hydrapple Protects, Earthquake still targets Empoleon; if Empoleon Protects, Ice Beam removes Hydrapple. Ally Earthquake damage is acceptable because preserving Blastoise while leaving both foes is less likely to win.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag confirmed. Opponent used Aerodactyl Wide Guard repeatedly beside Gengar and targeted Pelipper with Thunderbolt through turn 2. Mega Blastoise Dark Pulse can remove Gengar after Mega Evolution; Thunderbolt does not OHKO healthy Mega Blastoise. Opponent's disclosed back mode includes Empoleon/Hydrapple, while Dragonite and Arcanine were omitted in game 2. Future preview: evaluate a coherent mode that handles Gengar/Aerodactyl control while retaining strong answers into Empoleon/Hydrapple; do not assume alternate Mega formes. Snorlax can use Curse to build a physical endgame and Thick Fat checks listed Ice/Fire attacks.

decisions.rationale: Blastoise-Mega outspeeds Hydrapple and heavily threatens it with a 4x super-effective Ice Beam (87.8-152.1%). Hydrapple must Protect to block this threat safely. Empoleon (80 Speed) outspeeds Snorlax (-1 stage, 33-54 Speed) and can use rain-boosted Hydro Pump on Blastoise-Mega (39% HP), dealing 24.2-52.6% with a high probability to KO. Removing Blastoise leaves Snorlax isolated in a 2v1 against two special attackers targeting its unboosted Special Defense.

Blastoise is fainted, so its slot passes. Earthquake previously reduced Empoleon from full to 26% before Sitrus restored it to 51%, making another Earthquake the strongest available line and likely a KO. It also damages Hydrapple, while Curse or Body Slam gives Empoleon more opportunities to attack.
decisions.notebook: Mega Blastoise Dark Pulse can remove Mega Gengar after evolution. Opponent repeatedly paired Gengar with Aerodactyl Wide Guard and used Thunderbolt pressure. Opponent’s disclosed back mode includes Empoleon/Hydrapple; Dragonite and Arcanine were omitted in game 2. Snorlax’s Curse plus Thick Fat supports a physical endgame against listed Ice/Fire attacks. Evaluate future modes for Gengar/Aerodactyl control while retaining strong Empoleon/Hydrapple answers.

decisions.rationale: Snorlax is at +1 Atk and outspeeded by both our Pokémon. Snorlax's Earthquake will KO Empoleon at 51% HP. Protecting Empoleon completely denies Snorlax's KO while Hydrapple (100% HP, high Defense) safely chip-damages Snorlax with STAB Fickle Beam. Next turn, both Empoleon and Hydrapple can combine special attacks to finish Snorlax.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 2 roster revealed: Blastoise-Mega (Modest: Water Spout, Dark Pulse, Ice Beam, Protect), Pelipper (Modest, Leftovers, Drizzle: Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, U-turn, Protect), Houndoom (Timid, Life Orb, Flash Fire: Dark Pulse, Fire Blast, Sludge Bomb, Protect), Snorlax (Adamant, Sitrus Berry, Thick Fat: Curse, Rest, Body Slam, Earthquake). Lead Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl with Wide Guard completely shuts down Snorlax's Earthquake and Blastoise's Water Spout.

decisions.rationale: 1v2 with Snorlax slowest. Earthquake is the only move pressuring both foes: 2x SE on Empoleon and chip on Hydrapple. Body Slam into Empoleon is 0.5x NVE and leaves Hydrapple untouched. Curse further tanks Spe to no benefit; Rest opens two free turns of double-target hits at 54% HP.
decisions.notebook: Mega Blastoise and Pelipper and Houndoom all fainted in game 2. Opponent's Empoleon + Hydrapple endgame is the disclosed back mode; Dragonite and Arcanine were not brought in game 2. Snorlax CurseLax with Thick Fat remains the late-game closer; Earthquake is the cleanest answer to Water/Steel Empoleon and the only move that pressures a 1v2 field. For future modes, keep an Empoleon/Hydrapple answer (Ground or Dragon coverage) and respect Gengar + Aerodactyl Wide Guard pairing from game 1. Opponent's team uses consecutive Protect chains on Empoleon; consider status or double-target sequencing to break them.

decisions.rationale: Snorlax is the last remaining opposing Pokémon, at 53% HP and -1 Speed. Its full movepool is revealed (Curse, Body Slam, Earthquake, Rest) so it has no Protect. Both Empoleon (80 Speed) and Hydrapple (64 Speed) move before Snorlax (33-54 Speed). Combined Hydro Pump and Fickle Beam deals 46.0-77.0%, giving a high probability to KO Snorlax before it can move. Even on a miss, win is guaranteed on turn 8.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Game 2 roster: Blastoise-Mega (Modest), Pelipper (Modest, Leftovers, Drizzle), Houndoom (Timid, Life Orb, Flash Fire), Snorlax (Adamant, Sitrus Berry, Thick Fat: Curse, Rest, Body Slam, Earthquake). Lead Mega Gengar + Aerodactyl with Wide Guard completely counters Snorlax's Earthquake and Blastoise's Water Spout.

reflections.summary: Lost on team preview and lead math. Bringing Pelipper + Houndoom into a game where the opponent had Aerodactyl was a structural mistake — Rock Slide one-shot Houndoom turn 3 and forced Pelipper out shortly after, collapsing both the rain support and the Fire-type pressure before Snorlax could set up. Mega Blastoise was also a poor fit for the revealed Empoleon + Hydrapple endgame: Grass resists its Ice STAB (turn 5 Ice Beam was Protected and wasted), Empoleon's Hydro Pump chunked it from 40% to
reflections.adjustment: For game 3, abandon the Blastoise-Mega + Pelipper + Houndoom core here. Lead Snorlax with a Ground- or Dragon-type answer (Dragonite with Stomping Tantrum/Dragon Claw, or a dedicated Ground) so Earthquake coverage is live from turn 1 against Empoleon + Hydrapple. Do not double up on Rock-weak mons when Aerodactyl is still a threat, and either commit Curse on Snorlax turn 1 or use Rest+Body Slam as the slow pivot to actually reach the late game.
reflections.notebook: Opponent durables across series: Empoleon is Modest Sitrus with Competitive — sits around 50% and uses Protect + Hydro Pump as primary mode; pairs with Regenerator Hydrapple (Modest Leftovers) that runs Fickle Beam + Protect and can cheese physical walls. They lead Gengar-Mega + Aerodactyl together (game 1 Wide Guard shell, game 2 offensive lead) — Aerodactyl carries Focus Sash and is happy to trade Rock Slides. Empoleon + Hydrapple are the disclosed endgame back; Dragonite and Arcanine are their bench threats (Arcanine has Lum + Intimidate, Dragonite Life Orb Inner Focus Adamant). Counterplay notes: Wide Guard blanks Rock Slide/Earthquake, so sequence Ground and Rock moves on different turns; Empoleon chains Protect, so set Snorlax Curse after a confirmed Protect or double into a non-Protected turn; never bring two 4x-Rock-weak mons (Pelipper/Houndoom) when Aerodactyl is live. Team-preview lesson: against this Empoleon + Hydrapple + Aerodactyl core, prioritize a Ground-type and keep the CurseLax plan intact rather than pivoting to rain-Mega Blastoise which loses to Grass and out-ranged Water.

reflections.summary: The lead of Mega Gengar and Aerodactyl removed Houndoom early, while the bulky backline of Empoleon and Hydrapple comfortably outlasted Snorlax and Mega Blastoise in the late game.
reflections.adjustment: Anticipate Mega Blastoise targeting Mega Gengar with single-target coverage like Dark Pulse rather than relying on Wide Guard to protect Gengar.
reflections.notebook: Mega Blastoise carries single-target Dark Pulse and Ice Beam in addition to Water Spout. Snorlax relies on Earthquake, Body Slam, Curse, and Rest with Thick Fat. Empoleon and Hydrapple provide dominant defensive pressure into the Blastoise/Snorlax core.
